summary: The C case reaches the ordinary unarmed-target branch of apply.c:use_whip: a proficient Archeologist lashes a visible hostile soldier with no MON_WEP, and use_whip consumes the action through force_attack -> do_attack -> hitum. The JS replay stops before that behavior because uhitm.js:do_attack eagerly requires an unsupported callback; apply.js:use_whip calls force_attack without an operation environment. After removing that premature refusal, the active branch also needs its real capacity and overexertion operations wired. The intended bullwhip disarm branch is not reached.

source.branch: In apply.c:use_whip, a visible adjacent monster has MON_WEP == NULL; the hero is a proficient Archeologist (no fumbling or confusion), the target is hostile, and ordinary human melee proceeds through do_attack to hitum. force_attack temporarily sets forcefight for the hostile and returns do_attack result; use_whip returns ECMD_TIME when that result is true.
callers: cmd.c: command table maps the apply command a to doapply (line 1678)
apply.c:doapply selects BULLWHIP and dispatches to use_whip (4214-4232, 4265-4267)
apply.c:use_whip calls force_attack(mtmp, FALSE) in its no-MON_WEP branch (3245-3261)
dependencies: apply.c:use_whip requires wielded bullwhip, a direction, a visible adjacent target, proficiency, and the no-MON_WEP branch; its disarm branch is not reached.

uhitm.c:do_attack calls attack_checks, check_capacity, overexertion, exercise, u_wipe_engr, and hitum for the active human hostile path (515-582). The JS use_whip caller currently passes no env to force_attack, while do_attack requires checkCapacity and overexertion operations after its eager unsupported callback.

Other do_attack branches need their own C behavior and dependencies: safe peaceful/tame refusal (462-510), polymorph/noattacks and hmonas (524-529, 565-568), two-weapon teardown (536-537), and leprechaun evasion through m_move (555-563). This case does not evidence those branches.

evidence: nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1678 maps command a to doapply. nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:4214-4232 selects and validates the object, and 4265-4267 dispatches BULLWHIP to use_whip.

nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:2955-3003 defines use_whip setup and proficiency: Archeologist adds one proficiency level; DEX below 6, DEX at least 14, and Fumbling adjust it. The recorded fresh Archeologist has no Fumbling and is proficient; the adjacent hostile soldier is visible and has no MON_WEP.

nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:3127-3151 selects MON_WEP only for a visible known monster. With MON_WEP null, 3245-3258 emits the flick line and invokes force_attack; a true return immediately consumes the turn. The C recording challenges/cases/v10/bullwhip-lashes-unarmed-soldier.session.json at segment 0, zero-based step 23, key l, shows “You flick your bullwhip towards the soldier.  You lash the soldier.” and hitum RNG (rnd(20)=5); this is the lash/attack branch, not the intended disarm branch.

nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:432-443 sets forcefight for a hostile before calling do_attack and restores the prior value. Lines 448-583 show the ordinary attack path: after attack_checks and capacity/overexertion checks, a human hero reaches hitum and returns TRUE, which use_whip consumes.

At examined commit 395a168f14e2b9cdbcd5026f4597ce3b2f51c4bb, js/apply.js:817-831 calls force_attack(monster, false, state) at line 826 without env. js/uhitm.js:1160-1171 forwards its default empty env to do_attack. js/uhitm.js:1034-1039 throws “do_attack requires unsupported” at the eager require before checking the C branch; the evaluator records zero JS screens/RNG against C 24 screens and 3072 RNG. The exact command log is /tmp/teleport-loop-worker-c-20260925/.cache/C28-js-comparisons/bullwhip-lashes-unarmed-soldier.log.

The active branch has further unresolved production wiring: js/uhitm.js:1084-1090 requires checkCapacity and overexertion operations, and apply.js currently supplies neither through force_attack. The implementation scope should make the ordinary hostile path source-complete and correctly wire its production caller before claiming the function; preserve unsupported refusals only at genuinely unported source branches.
